review: Read the complete lifecycle card/helper and all thirteen tests. First-party React/TypeScript, synthetic process/profile/loopback fixtures; no runtime profile, credential, private transcript, game asset or third-party source copied.

Startup is an explicit operator action against a fixed same-origin endpoint. Saved loopback selection is validated before launch; operator_confirmation remains explicit. No arbitrary path, shell arguments or game action is exposed.

The helper links account changes and caller cancellation to request abort signals. Selection and launch deadlines are checked after response headers and JSON decoding before follow-up or result publication.

The card clears status on account changes, cancels on unmount and prevents stale result/error/finally handlers from changing the replacement operation. The helper also protects direct callers after it begins.
A typed startup receipt yields setup-completed text while awaiting game observation; partial server effects are shown when client setup fails. An incomplete success is rejected.

Existing account-policy source was reviewed in an earlier cohort. Shared lifecycle schemas are canonical test dependencies, outside this web export. These two files are copied with newline normalization only.
limits: Unfrozen unpublished source proposal; not a standalone application, installed acceptance or public release.
The lifecycle fix is newer than R379. Aborting renderer work does not terminate an already-admitted native launch, server or client.
HTTP is mocked. Tests do not prove EULA acceptance, installed mods, native server launch, Minecraft play, room delegation or GPT Live continuity.
The player panel and its corrected test need their own full source review. Work before another caller enters this helper remains that caller lifecycle responsibility.
